language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I'm Tim!
Hi, I'm Lisa and today I'm doing something really exciting. I'm going to spend the day with my Uncle Tom on his boat. I love the ocean!

It's crab season and we are going crab fishing. Crabs can only be caught during certain months of the year, we call this time crab season. This will allow them to mate, reproduce and increase their population in all the other months so that there will always be a supply of crab. I want to learn more about reproduction.
My uncle is a Vetenarian, so I'm sure he can explain a lot of things about animals.
Lisa would like to learn more about reproduction so let's help her. It's a beautiful day to go crab fishing, let's go!

Like humans, most animals and even many plants are either male or female. Males and females of the same species are a lot alike, but they also have some different features.
This is what a female crab looks like.
And this is what a male crab looks like.
Uncle Tom has caught a lot of crab and would like to sort them into their respective coolers. Blue cooler for male crabs and red cooler for female crabs. Can you help me?

Animals reproduce by either laying eggs or giving birth. Animals that give birth are called mammals and animals that lay eggs include birds, most reptiles, amphibians and fish.

Crabs reproduce by laying millions of eggs. That's a lot of eggs! Uncle Tom loves to take pictures of animals. He has lots of pictures just lying around the boat. He wants to put the pictures in a scrapbook according to how they reproduce. Can you help me?

Besides crabs, there are so many animals that live off the coast of California. My uncle and I have seen quite a few on our trip.
When animals reproduce they produce children that have similiar features and characteristics. This will ensure that their species will not die out or go extinct.
I took pictures of the animals I saw on our trip and need to match the offspring with their parents. Can you help me?

My uncle only goes crab fishing during certain months of the year. He says it's because otherwise you risk overfishing. Overfishing is when people fish so much that the animals cannot reproduce fast enough.
Then they will eventually die out.
That's frightening to think about. The possibility of no more crab! I'm very curious about that, so my uncle gave me a few questions to answer. Can you help me?
